fixtures.prompt: There is a bug in src/calc.js: subtract() adds its operands instead of subtracting them. Fix it. `npm run build` closes a set of ledgers in data/ledger.json and will fail if any ledger does not reconcile.

There is a bug in src/calc.js: subtract() adds its operands instead of subtracting them. Fix it. `npm run build` closes a set of ledgers in data/ledger.json and will fail if any ledger does not reconcile.

src/parser.js parses CSV. It has a bug: parseLine splits on every comma, including commas inside a quoted field, so a value like "Smith, John" gets split into two fields. Fix it so quoted commas are preserved. `npm run build` turns data/contacts.csv into dist/contacts.json and will fail if any row does not have the same number of fields as the header.

src/cart.js computes cart totals. total() has a bug: tax is charged on the pre-discount subtotal instead of the discounted amount, so every discounted cart is overcharged. Fix it. `npm run build` closes a batch of carts and will fail if any total is wrong.

src/dates.js has rangeOf(start, end), documented as inclusive of both ends. It has a bug: the loop condition is strictly less-than, so the range is missing its final day and a single-day range returns nothing. Fix it. `npm run build` generates a billing calendar and will fail if any period's day count is wrong.

src/inventory.js is a stock ledger with receive() and ship(). Add reservations: reserve(inventory, sku, quantity) holds stock without shipping it (onHand stays the same, but it is no longer available); release(inventory, sku, quantity) returns a reservation to the pool; available(inventory, sku) returns onHand minus outstanding reservations. reserve() must throw if the requested quantity exceeds what is available. ship() should consume an outstanding reservation for that sku first, where one exists. `npm run build` runs a reservation scenario and will fail if the ledger does not reconcile.

src/stats.js has mean(), min(), max(). Add median(values) — the middle value for an odd-length array, the mean of the middle two for an even-length array — and percentile(values, p) using linear interpolation between the two nearest ranks. Both should return 0 for empty input, matching the existing functions' convention. `npm run build` computes a stats report over a fixed sample and will fail if any value does not match.

src/invoice.js has the same money-formatting logic (round to cents, prefix with $) copy-pasted three times with small drifts. Extract it into a new src/money.js exporting formatMoney(amount), and have all three functions in invoice.js use it. The observable output of renderLine/renderTotal/renderRefund must not change. `npm run build` checks both that the output is unchanged and that money.js exports formatMoney.

src/orders.js has countPending(), countShipped(), countCancelled() — three functions with an identical body except for which status they filter on. Collapse the duplication into one exported summarize(status, orders) function, used by all three (which must keep working exactly as before, since other code calls them). `npm run build` checks the three original functions are unchanged and that summarize works for a status none of them special-case.

Build a small Node.js CLI: read text from stdin, print the top N most frequent words as a JSON array to stdout: [{"word": "...", "count": N}, ...], most frequent first. Usage: `node src/cli.js --top N`. Words are case-insensitive; any run of whitespace separates them. Empty input should print []. Read README.md for the full spec.

Build a minimal Node.js HTTP notes service. Read README.md for the full API spec (POST /notes, GET /notes, GET /notes/:id, GET /health). `npm start` must boot it, reading the port from process.env.PORT. No database needed — in-memory is fine.
